close_reason: Landed jscalendar-types slice in commit 3e27837. 10 enumerated-string sites → 8 typed enums via impl_string_enum! macro; 18 round-trip tests added; consumer crate tests updated. Parallel jscontact-types propagation filed as JMAP-sc1b.108 with human label pending design call on the no-JMAP-dep constraint conflict.
description:
Sites in crate-jmap-jscalendar-types/src/lib.rs where RFC 8984 enumerates a closed set of string values but the Rust type is bare `String`:

- line 123:  NDay.day                 — "mo"/"tu"/"we"/"th"/"fr"/"sa"/"su"
- line 144:  RecurrenceRule.frequency — "yearly"/"monthly"/"weekly"/"daily"/"hourly"/"minutely"/"secondly"
- line 156:  RecurrenceRule.skip      — "omit"/"backward"/"forward"
- line 160:  RecurrenceRule.first_day_of_week — same 7 day values as NDay.day
- line 232:  Location.relative_to     — "start"/"end"
- line 379:  Participant.kind         — "individual"/"group"/"location"/"resource"
- line 394:  Participant.participation_status — RFC 8984 enumerates ~6 values
- line 406:  Participant.schedule_agent — "server"/"client"/"none"
- line 474:  OffsetTrigger.relative_to — "start"/"end"
- line 569:  Alert.action             — "display"/"email"

Each could be an `#[non_exhaustive] enum` with `#[serde(rename_all = "camelCase")]` and the enumerated variants. Section 1 type-design: "Stringly-typed values where a newtype, enum, or validated wrapper would make invalid states unrepresentable."

Why this is opinion-tagged (not a P2 bug):
- The crate's PLAN.md design rationale documents intentional use of `String` to "preserve forward-compatibility with new sub-object types" (for `@type`) — and a similar argument applies to RFC 8984's general open-world model (the spec leaves room for vendor extensions). Today's RFC 8984 values are fixed, but a future RFC might add a frequency mode.
- An `#[non_exhaustive] enum` with an explicit `Unknown(String)` variant solves the forward-compat objection cleanly: known variants are typed, unknown values round-trip in the catch-all. But this turns a derive(Serialize, Deserialize) into a manual impl per enum, which is a maintenance cost.

Engineering basis (why not pure taste):
- Typos at construction site: `day: "mn".to_owned()` is accepted today, would be a wire-protocol violation. With an enum, the typo is a compile error.
- Documentation lives next to the type: a consumer reading `Frequency` immediately sees the 7 values; reading `String` requires going to RFC 8984.

Triage note: workspace AGENTS.md says "Sloppy-Value pattern for IETF-defined nested objects" is the workspace convention for value shapes "defined by an external IETF spec ... and is large or extensible". These are small fixed enums, not large/extensible value shapes — they are NOT covered by the sloppy-value exemption. Still, the call is a tradeoff between strict type-checking and forward-compat; reasonable Rust practitioners would split on this.

Filed as opinion-tagged so the loop converges and the call lands with the human, not the agent.
notes:
Parallel sites also exist in crate-jmap-jscontact-types/src/lib.rs — Anniversary.kind (line 854: "birth"/"death"/"wedding"), Phone.kind, Address.contexts keys, NameComponent.kind, etc. Same engineering argument and same forward-compat caveat apply. Treat as one finding spanning both type crates: if .77 is accepted, fix in jscalendar-types first (canonical extension-types pattern for the workspace's RFC-typed extraction crates), then propagate to jscontact-types.
Decision (2026-05-11, Mark): apply the canonical workspace 'same shape' pattern uniformly — convert each enumerated-string field to a `#[non_exhaustive] enum + Unknown(String) with #[serde(other)]` typed enum.

This is the same mechanism JMAP-lbdy already mandates for result enums (mechanism 2). Known RFC 8984 / RFC 9553 variants are typed; future spec or vendor values round-trip via Unknown(String). The forward-compat concern raised in the bead body is fully resolved by the Unknown variant.

Scope (per bead description + notes):
  1. jscalendar-types canonical first: NDay.day, RecurrenceRule.frequency, RecurrenceRule.skip, RecurrenceRule.first_day_of_week (alias of NDay.day), Location.relative_to, Participant.kind, Participant.participation_status, Participant.schedule_agent, OffsetTrigger.relative_to, Alert.action.
  2. Propagate to jscontact-types parallel sites: Anniversary.kind, Phone.kind, NameComponent.kind, AddressComponent.kind, Address.contexts (keys), etc.

Each new enum carries #[non_exhaustive] and round-trip tests (known variant + Unknown(String) variant).

Removing 'human' label so the autonomous /do-beads loop can pick this up.
Superseded (2026-05-11, Mark): this conversion is being reverted. See JMAP-sc1b.111 (the revert bead) and JMAP-sc1b.110 (the workspace AGENTS.md policy narrowing that makes this conversion out-of-scope).

Reason: RFC enumerations of classifier strings on data-object sub-types in externally-owned-schema-mirror type crates (jscalendar-types, jscontact-types) do not reflect operational reality. Real-world wire traffic routinely contains values outside the RFC enumeration. Typed enums with Other(String) catch-all create fiction; the catch-all does the work, the named variants do not. Maintenance cost is paid for no programmatic benefit.

This bead stays closed (it shipped successfully; the work was real). The policy call that made it the wrong posture came later.
title: P3: jscalendar-types enumerated-string fields (frequency, day, kind, action) could be enums
